families.s: HSE prevention of occupational dermatitis in food work
families.t: wet work, detergents, foods, irritants, allergens, gloves, skin checks, early reporting
f: Work-related skin disease is preventable through exposure control and suitable skin protection.
Employers should identify skin hazards and provide advice, training and appropriate controls.
Gloves should be selected for the chemical, task, duration and wearer.
Food disinfectants can irritate or sensitise the skin, eyes and respiratory system.
Skin exposure can occur while mixing, spraying, wiping or removing contaminated PPE.
Washing facilities should be readily available before eating and after chemical work.
Fruit, vegetables and cleaning chemicals are recognised dermatitis sources in food processing.
Early symptoms should be reported so exposure and controls can be reviewed.

families.s: HSE control of damaging noise in food and drink manufacture
families.t: machinery noise, assessment, engineering control, enclosures, damping, maintenance, hearing protection, surveillance
f: Hearing loss caused by work is preventable.
Employers should assess exposure and comply with the Control of Noise at Work Regulations.
Equipment should be selected and designed to reduce noise risk.
Food processes can exceed levels at which employers must take action.
Milling, drinks production and meat processing can generate particularly high noise.
Engineering controls include enclosure, damping, screens, silencers and anti-vibration mounts.
Good maintenance can prevent rattles and noise caused by wear.
Hearing protection and health surveillance may be needed after engineering controls are applied.

families.s: HSE management of work-related stress in food manufacturing
families.t: demands, control, support, relationships, role, change, risk assessment, action
f: Work-related stress should be managed through risk assessment and action.
HSE's Management Standards provide a structured approach.
Excessive demands and low control can contribute to stress-related ill health.
Support, relationships, role clarity and organisational change are relevant risk areas.
Employers should identify organisational causes rather than relying only on individual coping.
Employees should know how to raise concerns and access support.
Control measures should be reviewed for effectiveness.
Food-sector case studies demonstrate that practical organisational changes can improve worker outcomes.

families.s: HSE control of disinfectant exposure in food and drink production
families.t: COSHH, compatibility, dilution, CIP, spraying, fogging, PPE, surveillance and emergency response
f: Food disinfectants are hazardous substances and can harm workers by inhalation, ingestion or contact.
COSHH assessments should list chemicals, hazards, controls, monitoring and emergency arrangements.
Incompatible chemicals should be separated because mixing can release toxic gas or create violent reactions.
Working concentrations should not exceed the manufacturer's specification.
Automatic metering or pre-diluted products are safer than manually tipping concentrates.
Clean-in-place systems can minimise operator exposure when maintained and used correctly.
Mist spraying and fogging generate aerosols and may require RPE, PPE and controlled re-entry.
Application equipment, exposure controls and protective equipment require inspection and maintenance.

families.s: HSE safety and occupational-health priorities in meat, poultry and fish processing
families.t: powered knives, saws, refrigeration, zoonoses, fish proteins, smoke, cold work, handling
f: Meat, poultry and fish processing combines machinery, knife, handling and cold-work hazards.
Powered saws, bowl choppers and packing machinery can create serious injury and noise risks.
Blast freezers and chillers contribute to cold and noise exposure.
Micro-organisms such as Campylobacter can present infection risks in poultry processing.
Fish proteins can cause occupational asthma in exposed workers.
Smoking meat or fish can create exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons.
Long-term work at reduced temperatures can cause ill health.
Machine access, cleaning and blockage clearance require effective guarding and isolation.
